**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

The IP/data bargain sits at our **preferred** position, so there is nothing to redline:

- **Deliverables ownership + assignment** — § 14.2: we own each Deliverable on creation (subject to payment), with a present assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest, personnel assignments and further assurances. "Deliverable" (§ 1.4) covers work product created specifically for us.
- **Vendor keeps only its own pre-existing IP** — § 14.3 / § 1.9: Vendor Technology is its pre-existing software, tools, models and templates, expressly excluding Customer Data and IP we owned before the Effective Date.
- **Licence back to embedded Vendor IP** — § 13.2: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" licence to use, modify, create derivative works and have contractors support the material for our business; § 14.3 routes embedded Vendor Technology to it, and § 10.1 preserves it post-termination.
- **Customer Data** — § 14.1 (we own all Customer Data and our independent IP; Vendor gets a limited processing right only), reinforced by § 15.1 (no sale, advertising, commingling or model training without our written consent) and §§ 11.2–11.3 (return and deletion).
- **No joint ownership** — § 14.4, which also keeps feedback voluntary and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback.

No assignment or broad licence of our IP or data to Vendor appears anywhere (checked §§ 12, 16, 24, 25 as well). Noted in the rationale but not flagged: § 13.3's narrow suspension right during a material uncured payment/use breach after notice and cure, and the anonymized-telemetry carve-out in the Customer Data definition — both customary and immaterial here.
